current_strengths: The claim-kind vocabulary is centralized in SUPPORTED_ATOMIC_CLAIM_KINDS and the policy matrix fails fast if policy rows or policy details drift from that set.

The policy layer is explicit and compact: each claim kind has a lane, allowed surfaces, required fields, runtime_lowerable flag, default suppression reason, operator meaning, and diagnostic-only operator impact.

The surface gates are separated from policy text and enforce exact surface boundaries: Mulligan accepts only mulligan_keep or mulligan_discard, GlobalValues accepts gameplan_posture but rejects globalvalue_numeric_tuning until runtime evidence, Combo accepts combo_sequence, and CardID accepts supported per-card semantic claims.

The Darkbishop-style failure mode is directly guarded: hero_power_transform can remain effect-visible on CardID surfaces while start-of-game non-hand effects are rejected as opening-hand Mulligan keeps.
The builder/router layer is not inferred from documentation; conformance runs representative claims through the actual Mulligan, GlobalValues, CardID, and Combo builder/router functions.

The conformance snapshot distinguishes unexpected contract drift from legitimate builder prerequisite gaps. The current known gap is combo_sequence with an incomplete sequence, exposed as sequence_too_short rather than as a policy or gate failure.
source_contract_audit.json gives per-claim lifecycle rows from policy lane through surface gate, builder/router decision, runtime surface, emitted files, suppression reason, and first missing link.
source_to_runtime_explainability.json gives a card-readable projection of the same diagnostic chain and keeps apply_blocking=false.
contract_spine_rows provide the requested compact source -> policy -> surface gate -> builder/router -> runtime effect chain and intentionally exclude apply authority fields.

contract-spine-sentinel adds a repo-level no-second-gate guardrail by detecting policy/spine coverage drift, apply-authority fields in diagnostic rows, non-diagnostic operator impact, missing start-of-game suppression, and diagnostic consumers in active apply paths.

The active apply boundary is independently guarded: apply_gate.py and runtime_apply.py depend on operator_summary.json and package structure, not source_contract_audit.json, source_to_runtime_explainability.json, contract_spine_rows, or claim_lifecycle_rows.
Docs and tests agree that contract-spine-sentinel is developer diagnostic tooling, not the normal operator path and not an apply gate.
Focused verification passed against the current implementation, including sentinel, conformance, freeze, audit, explainability, and apply-authority boundary tests.
gaps_or_risks: The contract spine is strong for current claim kinds, but it depends on future claim-kind additions updating four boundaries together: SUPPORTED_ATOMIC_CLAIM_KINDS, source_contract_matrix.py, the matching surface gate, and builder/router or diagnostic coverage.

The conformance snapshot uses representative synthetic claims, so it proves contract alignment and builder/router expectations, not exhaustive real-deck behavior for every possible claim payload shape.

Some CardID lowering remains conditional by design. Claims such as card_role, mechanic_usage, known_bad_pattern, discover_choice, and choose_one_choice can pass the CardID surface gate but still suppress at the router when exact runtime block, mechanic policy, option identity, or condition prerequisites are missing.

Combo lowering correctly exposes incomplete sequence prerequisites, but that means a surface gate allowed decision alone is insufficient to imply runtime emission. Operators and future code must keep reading builder/router outcome fields.

source_contract_audit.py intentionally treats policy-matrix failure as non-blocking diagnostic degradation, mapping policy lanes to unsupported_or_unmapped. That preserves no-block operation but could hide a developer drift until sentinel or tests are run.

The sentinel scans configured active apply paths for diagnostic-only tokens. If future runtime-write code is added outside ACTIVE_APPLY_PATHS without updating the sentinel, the no-second-gate scan would not cover that new path.

Line-of-defense coverage is currently focused and strong, but broad full-suite regressions were not run for this audit. The focused contract-spine slice is sufficient for the requested spine audit, not a whole-repo release signal.
The schema requested only audit-level fields, so this artifact records findings and evidence rather than embedding the full generated contract_spine_rows payload.
recommended_next_actions: Keep the current architecture; do not introduce another apply gate or approval artifact from source_contract_audit.json, source_to_runtime_explainability.json, contract_spine_rows, or contract-spine-sentinel.

When adding any claim kind, require one small PR checklist item that updates SUPPORTED_ATOMIC_CLAIM_KINDS, source_contract_matrix.py, live surface-gate behavior, and builder/router or diagnostic tests in the same change.

Extend ACTIVE_APPLY_PATHS in contract_spine_sentinel.py whenever a new runtime-write or apply-authority code path is introduced, so the no-second-gate scanner continues covering all active mutation paths.

Keep source_contract_audit.py policy-matrix failure non-blocking for operators, but ensure CI or developer workflows run contract-spine-sentinel so developer drift is caught before it reaches normal package builds.

For the next maintenance pass, add a generated or snapshot-style developer report that stores the current contract_spine_rows output for easier human diff review, while keeping it diagnostic-only and outside apply authority.
If real-deck runs expose repeated CardID suppressions, add targeted router tests and mechanic-specific lowering policies rather than widening policy lanes or weakening surface gates.
no_blocking_constraints: operator_summary.json must remain the single normal runtime apply authority.
contract-spine-sentinel must remain diagnostic-only and must not become a normal operator path, a runtime writer, or a prerequisite for applying a valid package.
source_contract_audit.json, source_to_runtime_explainability.json, contract_spine_rows, and claim_lifecycle_rows must explain source-to-runtime decisions but must not grant or deny apply permission.

ALLOWED_WITH_WARNINGS and load_safe_apply must continue to allow technically valid packages even when source depth, unsupported mechanics, runtime-evidence-required tuning, or builder prerequisite gaps are visible.

Technical hard blocks should remain technical: invalid package structure, invalid JSON, missing operator_summary.json, missing required GlobalValues.json or Mulligan.json, undeclared runtime files, unsupported optional runtime surfaces in the normal path, forged gates, and invalid technical_status must stop apply.
Surface gate allowed must not be treated as runtime emission. Builder/router decisions and emitted file evidence must remain separate diagnostics.

Start-of-game effects, hero-power transforms, deckbuilding effects, and broad card-importance language must not become Mulligan keeps unless an explicit mulligan_keep or mulligan_discard claim separately supports opening-hand behavior.
globalvalue_numeric_tuning must remain runtime-evidence-required in Step 1; source-only numeric tuning should be visible but suppressed until fresh runtime evidence exists.
Presume.json and Concede.json must stay outside the normal HSConfig output/apply path unless the project deliberately changes that runtime-surface policy.
Future diagnostics may add clearer explanations, but they must not add another source-depth, conformance, or sentinel gate in front of valid load-safe apply.
